transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I've started catching myself having some pretty heavy thoughts lately. I keep thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes, on the drive home from school, I actually start wondering if my family and my students would just be better off without me. It really scares me to think that way, because I don't want to act on it or hurt myself, but the thoughts are there. So, I knew I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Have you made a specific plan for how you would harm yourself?

No, I haven't. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I really don't want to act on it. I don't actually want to hurt myself. It's just... those thoughts keep popping up, you know? Just wishing I wouldn't wake up, or thinking my family and my students would be fine without me. But no, I haven't made any sort of plan to actually do anything.
Have you ever had a distinct period when you felt unusually energized or irritable compared with your usual self?

No, I haven't. I mean, I don't think so. I've never really felt like I had a lot of extra energy or anything like that. Just... kind of the opposite, really. I've just been feeling so down. But no, no periods of feeling unusually energized or overly irritable like you're asking about.
How long have you been feeling down?

It's been going on for a while now. About a year and seven months, I think. It started right around the time I took over the STEM assessment redesign at school, which was on top of my regular teaching load. I've just felt this way ever since then.
During this period, have you lost interest in or stopped enjoying activities that you usually find pleasurable?

Yes, definitely. I used to really look forward to things, you know? Like, I play in a softball league, and I'm in a book club... I have a garden I used to love working in, and I run the robotics club at school. But lately, I just... I mostly just go through the motions. Or I end up canceling on people. None of it really feels enjoyable anymore. I just don't have the interest I used to.
During this period, have you often felt unusually tired or low on energy?

Yes, definitely. By the time I get through a day of teaching and a department meeting, my body just feels so heavy. It's like... even doing basic things, like making dinner or trying to answer a few parent emails, it just feels like climbing a hill. I just don't have the energy for it anymore.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions during this period?

Yeah, I have. It's actually been really frustrating at work. Um... I’ll sit there and read the same student response three or four times, and I just still won't know what score to give it. It's like my brain just won't process it. And making decisions is just as bad. Even really simple choices, like figuring out which lab supplies to order, can end up stalling me for an hour.
During this period, have you often felt worthless or excessively guilty about things?

Yes, I have. Um... if a lesson goes badly at school, or even if just one student looks confused, I immediately take it as proof that I’m letting everyone down. I just keep replaying it in my head over and over. It makes me feel like I'm a terrible teacher, and... and a terrible mother, too. I just feel guilty all the time, like I'm failing everyone who depends on me.
How has your sleep been during this period?

It hasn't been good. Um... even when I'm completely exhausted, I'll just lie awake in bed. I keep replaying assessment deadlines or, you know, mistakes I made in the classroom that day. And then, when I do manage to fall asleep, I usually end up waking up around 4 a.m., and... I never really get back to sleep after that.
